question: Should OpenClaw intentionally remove all approval-free `jq` execution from `tools.exec.safeBins`, including simple field filters that current main allows?
rationale: This is a security hardening of the exec approval boundary, but it is also an upgrade-visible compatibility change for operators who explicitly configured `jq` as a safe bin.

options.title: Accept fail-closed jq safeBins
options.body: Treat `jq` as outside the stdin-only safe-bin model and merge after real behavior proof and release-note context confirm the upgrade behavior.

options.title: Preserve current jq filters
options.body: Keep simple `jq` filters eligible for safeBins and pursue narrower parser hardening for modules/startup/env behavior instead.

options.title: Pause for policy redesign
options.body: Hold the PR until a maintainer-owned safe-bin policy update decides whether broad tool-specific parsers belong in this surface at all.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed jq safeBins
recommendation.body: Treat `jq` as outside the stdin-only safe-bin model and merge after real behavior proof and release-note context confirm the upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest commit history on the safe-bin policy and jq hardening path this PR changes.
